era_benchmark_plan.benchmark_rationale: SPY is the standard broad US equity benchmark for a STOCKS-sleeve regime-aware momentum strategy. The strategy gates entries on SPY's own trend (200-day MA), so SPY is both the regime filter anchor and the natural performance baseline. Beating SPY on a risk-adjusted basis is the minimum bar for a momentum strategy that is sometimes flat/cash.

eras.label: Late-cycle bull market (2018–2019)
eras.rationale: A sustained risk-on environment with periodic volatility spikes (Q4 2018 drawdown). Tests whether the SPY 200-day MA filter correctly keeps the strategy invested during recoveries and flat during the Q4 2018 correction.

eras.label: COVID crash and V-recovery (2020)
eras.rationale: The fastest bear-to-bull transition in modern history. A critical stress test for the regime filter: the strategy should go flat near the crash trough and re-enter during the recovery. Failure here would indicate the 200-day MA filter lags too severely.

eras.label: Post-COVID momentum bull (2021)
eras.rationale: Strong broad-market momentum with high cross-sectional dispersion — the most favorable environment for a momentum strategy. Establishes an upper-bound performance reference.

eras.label: Rate-shock bear market (2022)
eras.rationale: Sustained drawdown driven by Fed tightening. The regime filter should push the strategy to cash for extended periods. Tests capital preservation and whether the stop-loss bounds prevent catastrophic drawdown when the filter is slow to trigger.

eras.label: Recovery and AI-driven bull (2023–2024)
eras.rationale: A momentum-friendly environment with concentrated leadership (mega-cap tech/AI). Tests whether the large-cap liquid universe screen captures the dominant momentum names and whether the 60-day lookback is responsive enough.

eras.label: Recent validation window (2025–present)
eras.rationale: The most recent tape. Validates that the strategy is still relevant and has not decayed. Required by Vires readiness gates before paper promotion. Kept as a separate era to avoid in-sample contamination from the longer historical eras.

60-day anchor accepted via ACCEPT_DEFAULT on clarify_02_clarify_momentum_lookback. Sweep spans 20/60/120 to bracket short-, medium-, and intermediate-term momentum without excessive overfitting surface. Step of 20 yields 6 variants.

SPY 200-day MA regime filter accepted as default via clarify_01_clarify_regime_filter ACCEPT_DEFAULT. A secondary 150-day variant is included to test sensitivity without widening the surface materially. Yields 2 variants.

Stop-loss range of 5–15% accepted via proposed default on clarify_05_clarify_stop_loss_target. Expressed as positive magnitude; engine applies as negative. Step of 5 yields 3 variants consistent with balanced risk profile and SMALL capital tier.

Profit-target range of 10–25% accepted via proposed default on clarify_05_clarify_stop_loss_target. Step of 5 yields 4 variants. Combined with stop-loss variants, cross-product is bounded by max_total_variants.

trial_ledger_budget.rationale: Sweep space is defined by three primary axes: momentum lookback (3 values: 20, 60, 120 days), stop-loss level (4 values: -5%, -8%, -12%, -15%), and profit target (2 values: +15%, +25%), yielding 3 × 4 × 2 = 24 total variants. Four eras span the 2018–2026 window (pre-COVID bull, COVID crash/recovery, 2022 bear, 2023–2026 recovery), so max_bench_runs = 24 × 4 = 96. This is a conservative budget: the lookback sweep is bounded to three academically motivated anchors rather than a fine grid, and stop/target levels are coarse enough to avoid excessive overfitting surface while still covering the balanced risk profile. Compute cost is estimated at $0.00 because all signals are OHLCV-derived from alpaca_equity_daily_ohlcv with no external API fees. The budget is internally consistent: max_variants (24) equals sweep_bounds.max_total_variants and max_bench_runs (96) equals max_variants × max_eras. Server normalization: Server raised the trial-ledger budget to cover 48 variants across 6 eras after sectioned Talon synthesis.

multiple_comparisons_plan.notes: Sweep space spans 3 momentum lookback variants (20d, 60d, 120d) × 3 stop-loss levels (5%, 10%, 15%) × 4 profit-target levels (10%, 15%, 20%, 25%) = 36 effective parameter combinations across 4 eras. Bonferroni correction applied: α_adjusted = 0.05 / 36 ≈ 0.0014. All clarification answers were accepted defaults (TUNABLE_DEFAULT provenance); operator has not confirmed any parameter anchor, so the full sweep surface must be penalized. The known-good regime-aware momentum template used bounded stop/target sweeps with an explicit overfitting guard — this plan respects that lesson. If the operator later pins the lookback to 60d (the proposed default), effective_trials_estimate drops to 12 and adjusted_significance_level rises to ~0.0042.

checks.finding: Entry and exit rules are explicitly scaffolded placeholders with compiler_support='NEEDS_MAPPING'. No concrete signal logic exists to audit for lookahead. The momentum lookback sweep references a condition path 'entry_rules.value.conditions[momentum_lookback].threshold' that does not correspond to any implemented condition in the scaffolded entry_rules block. Without actual signal computation logic, it is impossible to confirm that trailing returns, moving averages, or regime filters are computed strictly on prior-bar data. The strategy_spec section failed Talon validation 3 times and was replaced by a server scaffold — meaning no reviewable signal implementation exists.
checks.remediation: A complete, compiler-valid strategy_spec with explicit signal definitions (e.g., trailing return computed on close[t-1] through close[t-61], SPY SMA computed on prior bars only) must be produced and validated before this packet can proceed. Lookahead safety cannot be assessed on a scaffold.

checks.finding: The packet explicitly acknowledges in assumptions (field_path: strategy_spec.universe_screen.survivorship_bias, confidence: HIGH) that the universe screen using fundamentals_basic ADV metadata is NOT point-in-time. The current S&P 500 / large-cap constituent list is used as the screening pool rather than the historical constituent list at each rebalance date. This is a confirmed, operator-acknowledged survivorship bias that will inflate backtest returns across all six eras, particularly the 2018–2022 window where constituent turnover was material. The data_readiness block shows alpaca_equity_daily_ohlcv as BLOCKED with no catalog entry matched, meaning the actual data coverage and constituent history cannot be verified.
checks.remediation: Replace the current-snapshot fundamentals_basic screen with a point-in-time constituent list (e.g., historical S&P 500 membership by date) or explicitly restrict the backtest universe to a fixed list of symbols that were large-cap liquid throughout the entire historical window and document the resulting look-forward exclusion. Alternatively, apply a survivorship-bias haircut to all reported metrics with a documented methodology. This must be resolved before any backtest results are treated as evidence.

checks.finding: The execution_constraints block sets commission_assumption_value=0 (flat, zero commission) and slippage_assumption_bps=10. For a DAYS-horizon momentum strategy trading 10–50 large-cap names with daily or per-signal rebalancing, 10 bps one-way slippage with zero commission is likely an underestimate, particularly for smaller names within the 10–50 symbol dynamic screen. The commission model is 'FLAT' at $0, which does not reflect realistic broker costs for a SMALL capital tier account. Additionally, the universe rebalance_frequency is 'per_bench_run' which is undefined in terms of calendar frequency — if this implies daily rebalancing, round-trip costs compound significantly. The trial_ledger_budget notes $0 compute cost, which is plausible for OHLCV signals but does not address trading cost sensitivity.
checks.remediation: Set commission_assumption_value to a realistic per-trade or per-share cost (e.g., $0.005/share or $1/trade minimum). Increase slippage_assumption_bps to at least 15–20 bps for a DAYS-horizon strategy. Define rebalance_frequency in calendar terms. Run a cost-sensitivity sweep showing strategy viability at 2x and 3x assumed costs before promotion.

checks.finding: SPY is used as both the regime filter anchor (200-day MA gate) and the performance benchmark. This dual role is disclosed and rationale is provided in era_benchmark_plan. The benchmark is sourced from the same data feed (alpaca_equity_ohlcv) as the strategy signals, so no look-ahead from a separate benchmark feed is introduced. The benchmark choice (SPY) is appropriate for a large-cap US equity momentum strategy. No evidence of benchmark selection post-hoc or cherry-picking of comparison period.

The primary data input alpaca_equity_daily_ohlcv has data_readiness status BLOCKED — 'No catalog entry matched alpaca_equity_daily_ohlcv.' This means no actual data has been confirmed available for the 2018-01-01 to 2026-05-05 window. All sweep bounds, era plans, and evidence thresholds are constructed against a data source whose availability, coverage, and quality are unverified. Furthermore, the strategy_spec failed validation and was scaffolded by the server, meaning the signal-to-data mapping (which data fields feed which signals) has never been validated. The fundamentals_basic data used for universe screening is acknowledged as non-point-in-time, creating a form of future-data leakage into the universe construction step. The recent_validation era ends 2026-05-05, which is beyond any plausible current date for a strategy authored in this window — the end date should be confirmed as not exceeding actual available data.
checks.remediation: Resolve the data_readiness BLOCKED status by confirming a matched catalog entry for alpaca_equity_daily_ohlcv with verified coverage dates before any bench run. Replace non-point-in-time fundamentals_basic universe screening with a point-in-time source or fixed list. Confirm the recent_validation era end date does not exceed actual data availability. Produce a compiler-valid strategy_spec with explicit data field mappings before implementation.

checks.finding: The era plan covers six distinct regimes from 2018 to 2026: late-cycle bull (2018–2019), COVID crash and V-recovery (2020), post-COVID momentum bull (2021), rate-shock bear (2022), AI-driven recovery bull (2023–2024), and a recent validation window (2025–present). This provides meaningful regime diversity including bull, bear, crash, recovery, rising rates, and high-volatility environments. The regime_expectation=MOST_CONDITIONS is appropriately interpreted as bull-regime participation with cash during bear regimes. The SPY 200-day MA filter is tested across regime transitions. Era weighting is equal, which is reasonable for a first-draft strategy.

The operator-supplied kill_criteria_user is the string 'test' — explicitly acknowledged as a placeholder with no substantive kill rule. The packet notes that 'standard evidence-threshold-based kill criteria (drawdown breach, profit factor floor, trade count floor)' will govern, but these are generic thresholds (min_profit_factor=1.3, min_sharpe=0.6, max_drawdown=20%) applied at the backtest stage. There are no live-trading kill criteria defined: no maximum consecutive loss count, no regime-change trigger, no time-based decay check, no correlation-spike kill, and no explicit drawdown circuit breaker for live deployment beyond the scaffolded 'circuit_breaker_rules: Scaffolded risk guard; operator review required before promotion.' The paper and live evidence thresholds exist but are not connected to any automated kill mechanism in the spec.
checks.remediation: Replace the 'test' kill criteria placeholder with at least: (1) a maximum consecutive losing trade count (e.g., 5), (2) a rolling 30-day drawdown kill threshold for live trading, (3) a regime-change kill rule (e.g., if SPY crosses below 200-day MA and strategy is still holding positions, force exit within N days), and (4) a minimum trade frequency check to detect signal decay. These must be operator-confirmed, not scaffolded.

checks.finding: The sweep space is 48 variants across 6 eras (288 bench runs per trial_ledger_budget after server normalization), but the multiple_comparisons_plan uses Bonferroni correction calibrated to 36 effective combinations (3 lookbacks × 3 stop-loss × 4 profit-target), which is inconsistent with the 48-variant max_total_variants stated in sweep_bounds. The adjusted significance level of 0.0014 is extremely tight and may be unachievable given the evidence thresholds (min_sharpe=0.6, min_profit_factor=1.3), creating a situation where the strategy either fails the significance bar or the evidence bar — but this tension is not acknowledged. More critically: the strategy_spec is a server scaffold with no real signal logic, meaning the sweep is being designed around parameters that have no implemented counterpart. The 60-day lookback anchor was accepted as a default without operator research justification, and the entire parameter space was constructed from TUNABLE_DEFAULT provenance with no operator confirmation of any anchor. The pattern_description explicitly states 'I don't expect anything to work yet but we're going to spoof some data here' — this is a test packet with no genuine thesis, making any sweep result inherently uninterpretable as evidence of edge. The trial_ledger_budget rationale contains an internal inconsistency: it describes a 3×4×2=24 variant space in the rationale text but the server normalized to 48 variants, and the sweep_bounds parameters yield a different cross-product (6×2×3×4=144 if fully crossed), none of which match each other.
checks.remediation: This packet must not proceed to bench automation. The operator has explicitly stated this is a test with spoofed data and no real thesis. Before any sweep is run: (1) establish a genuine, research-backed thesis; (2) produce a compiler-valid strategy_spec; (3) resolve the internal inconsistency between sweep_bounds cross-product, max_total_variants, and trial_ledger_budget rationale; (4) confirm at least one parameter anchor with operator research justification rather than TUNABLE_DEFAULT provenance; (5) acknowledge the tension between the Bonferroni-adjusted significance level and the evidence thresholds.

adversarial_review.overall_notes: This packet is a self-described test submission with explicitly spoofed data and no genuine thesis ('I don't expect anything to work yet but we're going to spoof some data here'). It carries five critical or blocking deficiencies that independently justify FAIL status: (1) the primary data source alpaca_equity_daily_ohlcv is BLOCKED with no catalog match, making all backtest planning notional; (2) the strategy_spec failed Talon validation three times and was replaced by a server scaffold with NEEDS_MAPPING placeholders throughout — no reviewable signal logic exists; (3) survivorship bias from non-point-in-time universe screening is explicitly acknowledged at HIGH confidence but unmitigated; (4) the sweep parameter cross-product is internally inconsistent across three sections of the packet; and (5) the kill criteria is a literal placeholder string 'test'. The era plan and benchmark selection are the only structurally sound elements. No backtest results should be generated from this packet in its current state.
conditions_for_pass: 1. Resolve data_readiness BLOCKED status: confirm a matched catalog entry for alpaca_equity_daily_ohlcv with verified coverage dates spanning the intended historical window.
2. Produce a compiler-valid strategy_spec with no NEEDS_MAPPING placeholders: all entry conditions, exit rules, and position sizing must be fully specified and pass schema validation.
3. Replace non-point-in-time universe screening with a point-in-time constituent source or a fixed symbol list with documented survivorship-bias methodology and metric haircut.

4. Resolve the internal inconsistency between sweep_bounds cross-product, sweep_bounds.max_total_variants (48), multiple_comparisons_plan.effective_trials_estimate (48 vs 36), and trial_ledger_budget rationale (24 vs 48 variants).
5. Replace kill_criteria_user placeholder 'test' with substantive, operator-confirmed kill rules covering live drawdown, consecutive loss count, regime-change exit, and signal decay detection.
6. Establish a genuine investment thesis with research justification; this packet is explicitly a test with spoofed data and cannot produce interpretable evidence of edge.
